bull_bear.body:
- Market leader in most of its focused foundry-consumable product lines in India
- World-class proprietary technology, foundry-process expertise and product-application knowledge, drawn from global Vesuvius/Foseco group R&D
- Broad, diversified product portfolio spanning feeding, filtration, metal treatment, coatings, refractories, binders and simulation software
- Extensive application-engineering and technical-support capability backing customer solutions
- Robust reach across 21 Indian states plus exports to 12 countries, aiding customer proximity
- Expanded capabilities and global R&D synergies from the FCIL (formerly Morganite Crucible) acquisition, deepening non-ferrous/molten-metal-systems presence
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Geopolitical disruption in the Middle East (Strait of Hormuz) — Escalation around this strategically critical transit choke point has sharply raised global oil prices, increased energy-market volatility and transportation/logistics costs, and is estimated to reduce global trade growth by up to 0.5 percentage points - a downside risk particularly for energy-input-dependent, cross-border trade-reliant sectors such as the foundry industry the Company supplies.
- Global economic growth deceleration — Global GDP growth is projected to slow to 3.1% in 2026 from 3.4% in 2025, primarily attributed to persistent geopolitical tensions, which could dampen industrial and manufacturing demand across the trade-linked markets Foseco India's foundry customers serve.
- Rising input/energy cost and inflation pressure — India's CPI inflation for FY2026-27 is projected at 4.6%, reflecting pressures from recent increases in global energy prices driven by ongoing geopolitical tensions - a cost risk for an energy- and raw-material-intensive foundry-consumables manufacturer.
- Global financial-market and macro stability risk — Potential corrections in AI-related stock valuations and concerns over high public debt levels are explicitly flagged as contributing to downside risks to overall global economic stability.
- Climate/agricultural risk to food price stability — The potential onset of El Nino conditions poses a risk to agricultural output and food price stability, a factor relevant to India's broader inflation and domestic-demand backdrop that the Company's outlook is tied to.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Foseco India manufactures and supplies foundry consumables and equipment for iron, steel and non-ferrous foundries - feeding systems, filtration products, metal treatment, coatings, refractory products, binders/release agents and solidification-simulation software - serving foundries that in turn supply castings to automotive, tractors, M&HCV, 2-wheeler, general engineering, valves & pumps, power, railway, marine, construction and mining end-users. It operates across 21 Indian states and exports to 12 countries, and in FY2025 acquired a 75% stake in Foseco Crucible (India) Limited (formerly Morganite Crucible India Limited), expanding into molten metal systems and specialised crucible technologies for non-ferrous applications.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Feeding systems:** Insulating and exothermic feeding systems
- **Filtration products:** Filters for liquid iron, steel and aluminium
- **Metal treatment:** Inoculants and metal treatment products for ferrous and non-ferrous alloys, Degassing systems for aluminium, Rotoclene (steel metal cleaning)
- **Coatings:** Advanced coatings for sand moulds and cores, INSTA Coatings, ROTOCLENE, SEMCO CC Coatings, SEMCO FD Coatings, STELEX Optiflow, SPRAY Coating Systems
- **Refractory products:** Lining systems for ladles and furnaces, Crucibles and monolithic refractories, Stoppers and Nozzles for metal flow control, Segments and Skimming tools for metal treatment
- **Binders and release agents:** Environmentally friendly binders
- **Software solutions:** Solidification simulation software-based solutions

business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Integrate Foseco Crucible (India) Limited (FCIL, formerly Morganite Crucible India Limited) - bringing together complementary product portfolios, technical expertise and customer relationships across ferrous and non-ferrous segments, particularly Molten Metal Systems (MMS) crucible technologies
- Continue investment in technology, product development, process improvements and localisation initiatives aimed at improving operational efficiency and supporting customer needs
- Maintain cost discipline, enhance productivity and strengthen business resilience in a dynamic operating environment
- Leverage global R&D synergies and combined capability of the Vesuvius Group's global Foundry business for a broader product offering and enhanced customer reach
- Focus on operational excellence, customer-centricity and disciplined growth amid uncertain market conditions
- Dividend distribution follows the Company's Dividend Distribution Policy, framed per the parameters of Regulation 43A(2) of the SEBI Listing Regulations. The Board recommended maintaining the Final Dividend at Rs. 25 per share (250%) for FY2025, unchanged from FY2024, and did not propose transferring any amount to reserves - indicating a payout-oriented rather than reinvestment-heavy capital allocation stance for the year, alongside the FCIL acquisition being funded via a share swap (equity issuance) rather than cash/debt.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: FY2025 expansion centred on the acquisition of a 75% stake in Foseco Crucible (India) Limited (formerly Morganite Crucible India Limited), adding Molten Metal Systems (MMS) capabilities and specialised crucible technologies for non-ferrous metal applications, and bringing the acquired business under the Vesuvius Group's global Foundry business for combined R&D and customer reach. Separately, the Company continued investing in its R&D testing facility (Muffle furnace, Schimadzu Precision Universal Testing Machine, Tensometer, Insta Coatings) and in sustainability/energy-efficiency projects during 2025 operations - a split-oven project in Pune for energy efficiency and emissions reduction, replacement of an old vacuum pump in binders, replacement of an old air compressor in Puducherry, upgradation of Slurry Sleeves machines for energy efficiency, a Dust Extraction System, advanced flow meters for LPG monitoring, and improvements in Hydropulpers; in the prior year (2024) it had installed Retrofit Emission Control Devices (RECD) for all DG sets.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Demand across the foundry industry remained mixed during the year, influenced by fluctuations in global industrial activity, input cost movements, supply chain adjustments and changing customer requirements across automotive, infrastructure, engineering and manufacturing sectors
- Standalone revenue growth of 15.1% driven by strong demand, strategic pricing initiatives, volume growth and continued market expansion, with disciplined working capital management and cost control supporting profitability
- Policy-led import substitution (40% basic customs duty on Chinese iron castings effective January 2025) is compressing OEM ordering cycles and catalysing domestic manufacturing investment under Make in India/PLI
- EV-led demand: domestic EV production crossing 1 million units is driving aluminium HPDC components (battery enclosures, motor housings, structural frames); non-ferrous (aluminium) castings projected to grow at an 11.54% CAGR
- Mandatory Vehicle Scrappage Policy (operational from April 2025) is lowering melt costs 12-18% via cheaper scrap availability, while Industry 4.0/AI-led quality systems and energy-efficient induction melting are reshaping foundry operations
- Headwinds flagged: raw-material and energy cost volatility (petcoke/high-sulphur coal price rises), EU CBAM raising export costs from October 2025, Middle East geopolitical disruption affecting energy and logistics, and a highly fragmented MSME-dominated industry structure
- Indian foundry industry (USD 26.28bn in 2025) projected to grow to USD 28.72bn in 2026 and USD 46.72bn by 2031, supporting a favourable long-term demand backdrop for foundry consumable suppliers
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Foseco India is a global leader in high-performance foundry consumables and innovative technologies, and India's leading supplier of foundry consumables and solutions to ferrous and non-ferrous foundries.
